Both tables are owned by checksops_admin: the SQL 77 pre-apply inspect (SSM d6aaefb4-c337-4b85-865e-87e8b586d964) read table_owner and current_user checksops_admin for check_stakeholders, and the SQL 78 post-apply inspect (SSM 405d41e9-4b0e-4ca5-af90-27ff2c9428f2) read table_owner checksops_admin for check_partner_stakeholder_removals. The production rule (scripts/deployment-guard/lib/sql-member-stakeholder-production-apply.mjs, sql79) requires current_user to be expected_table_owner and authenticated not to be a member of it (recursive pg_auth_members, INHERIT FALSE and SET FALSE included) before; after, both tables' owner is still it and equals current_user, authenticated is still not a member, both tables' ACLs (every entry, the owner's own included) are unchanged, and the policies on the two tables are the ones before plus exactly the four aws_member_* policies (permissive, INSERT or DELETE, to authenticated). These reads sit beside the fingerprint, so d9bc8921… and 878d6441… are unchanged.
